children: UK stocks ended higher on Wednesday, supported by a rise in healthcare and consumer staples sectors, which gained on a weaker sterling after data showed US inflation came in hotter than expected.

Stronger-than-expected US inflation reading supported the dollar, lifting risk appetite for sectors benefiting heavily from export revenues

Meanwhile, UK Finance Minister John Healey is expected to pay for new initiatives with higher taxes or spending cuts rather than more borrowing, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, as the Iran war puts additional pressure on Britain's public finances
Homebuilders (.FTNMX402020) advanced 3.2% after Bank of England's chief economist Huw Pill said he is sceptical of market expectations for four rate hikes over the next year
"The BOE's caution is well established, and given the weakness of the labour market, any hike would be framed as insurance," said Geoff YU, senior EMEA markets strategist at BNY
